text: The returns run is the returns step of JOB-15, the daily reporting run of rwb-reporting at 01:30, on the task queue rwb-reporting; the step name, its order against the refresh step and the run record are local design, and no source names them.
why: The legacy story says only 'its trigger arrives' and the FSD A2.7.2 lists 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'; JOB-15 is the only job the Ownership Map gives rwb-reporting.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-001 Acceptance criteria; FSD P9 A2.7.2 and A2.1 AC-ALT-P9-001-01; _work/msr/context/P9.md (jobs: JOB-15)
confirm: Solution architect with the tech lead of rwb-reporting
impact: The return runs with the daily reporting run of the business date; a failure of the step holds the date and not the already frozen dates.

text: The regulatory return is the frozen measure snapshot set of a business date (measure_snapshot with frozen and published_at plus the measure_publish row) read through GET /reports/measures, and no data lake copy and no extract file is produced.
why: FSD A2.7.2 and TSD P9 T5.1 still name Power BI and the data lake, while Architecture v5 removes INT-19 and INT-20 and DP-17 moves reporting to events into rwb-reporting; the three owned tables already carry the frozen flag, the published_at and the publish status.
read: FSD P9 A2.7.2, A2.1 AC-ALT-P9-001-02 and AC-EXC-P9-001-03; TSD P9 T5.1 and T3.1; _work/msr/context/P9.md; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17, R8.4 ADR-018
confirm: Solution architect with the BI owner
impact: The regulator-facing number is read from this service's frozen rows; the lake and the 07:30 Power BI refresh receive nothing from this capability.

text: The measures of a return and their dimensions are data rows of measure_definition (data product from LOV-DATA-PRODUCT, unit from LOV-MEASURE-UNIT, dimension from LOV-MEASURE-DIM) with the definition version in force on the business date; no return layout table, no formula in code and no extra table is added, and the only parameter is a hold-on-stale switch named REPORTING_RETURNS_HOLD_ON_STALE, default true.
why: BR-P9-007 and TSD P9 NFR-065 forbid a business value in code, and the three owned tables already hold the definition, the value and the publish status; no source names a return layout or a parameter of the run.
read: FSD P9 A2.7.3.1 BR-P9-007 and VR-P9-007-1; TSD P9 T3.1, T3.2 and T7 NFR-065; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01
confirm: Data steward with the tech lead of rwb-reporting
impact: A new measure or a new dimension is a data change and not a release; the parameter name is local and reviewed at release.

text: The rule version in force is written with the returns decision through the local decision-record library on the shared rwb.decision-record.v1, and read back through the decision-log read of the rwb-decision contract; rwb-reporting keeps no copy of a rule package, a rule version or the ledger.
why: The legacy AC1 writes the result to the decision log with the rule version; DP-03 gives this service the local record and the shared topic, and the central ledger is rwb-decision's.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-001 AC1 and AC2; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03; R8.4 ADR-022
confirm: Owner of rwb-decision with the tech lead of rwb-reporting
impact: The return cites the rule version of the record; a refused record blocks the date and raises the incident of R-UNI-39.

text: The returns record carries FEAT-RPT-07 as its decision reference and a result of PUBLISHED or HELD, until the decision owner names a decision code for the capability.
why: No source names a decision code for a regulatory return, and a record without a reference cannot be traced to the feature that produced it.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-001 AC1; FSD P9 A1.2 FEAT-RPT-07; TSD P9 T3.2 LOV-MEASURE-PUBLISH
confirm: Owner of rwb-decision with the reporting owner
impact: A later decision code is an additive change to the element and does not change the frozen rows.

text: MSG-P9-002 and MSG-P9-003 are cited by their IDs only; this story does not write their text, which is set with the message standard owner.
why: Both IDs appear in the FSD exception flows and neither text exists in any extract read for this WP; inventing a text would put a business wording into a story.
read: FSD P9 A2.7.3.1 and A2.1 AC-EXC-P9-001-04 and A2.3 AC-EXC-P9-003-01; TSD P9 document control
confirm: Message standard owner with the business owner of P9
impact: The run record names the message ID; the wording arrives with the message standard and is a data change.

text: The read and the run use capability area Reporting with right R as TSD P9 T6.1 and T-A.1 give it, enforced through the platform authorisation path; DP-08 is not in the pattern set of this key, so no C dependency on rwb-access is added.
why: The legacy story names the monolith RecoveryAccessGuard and the TSD names the right; the pattern set of RWB-E8-001 is DP03, DP13 and DP19 only.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-001 Permission checks; TSD P9 T6.1 and T-A.1; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-08 and R5.7
confirm: Owner of rwb-access with the solution architect
impact: The refusal is MSG-P4-002 as the legacy story expects; the enforcement library is a platform concern and not a contract of this story.

text: A row of a published business date is frozen and is never rewritten; a late correction produces a new snapshot set for the corrected date and a correcting decision record naming the original, and the earlier frozen rows keep their value.
why: measure_snapshot.frozen is 'True when the row may not change', the FSD wants the baseline rows of an earlier date held unchanged, and R-UNI-24 requires a correcting record instead of an overwrite.
read: TSD P9 T3.1 DF-RPT-051 and DF-RPT-052; FSD P9 A2.1 AC-ALT-P9-001-02; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-24
confirm: Data steward with the tech lead of rwb-reporting
impact: A regulator sees two dated sets and one correcting record instead of a silent restatement.

text: The document_field entity of the legacy Data section is not read by this story, because documents belong to rwb-document, and the rule_row entity is not read either, because rule rows belong to rwb-decision; the return needs neither to produce a measure.
why: The legacy Data section lists document_field and rule_row as entities of a reporting story; the Ownership Map gives documents to P5 and rules to P7, and DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-001 Data; _work/msr/context/P9.md (three owned tables); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01
confirm: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-document and rwb-decision
impact: The return carries no document fact and no rule text; a future need is a new contract element and a new story.

text: The baseline declares GET /reports/measures (API-P9-001) under /api/recovery/reporting/v1 as its one provided operation and adds no second path for the return, because the Ownership Map gives rwb-reporting one provided operation.
why: TSD P9 T-A.1 has one row and the Ownership Map has one row; a second path would create a second owner of the same measure answer.
read: TSD P9 T-A.1 and T-A.2; _work/msr/context/P9.md (REST operations provided: GET /reports/measures); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-13
confirm: Solution architect with the API owner
impact: The return is read through the existing measure read; a regulator-specific path would need its own story and contract.

text: The Measure answer is a closed set of measureCode, name, definitionVersion, businessDate, productGroup, dimensionCode, dimensionValue, value, caseCount, unit and frozen, one row per measure and dimension value, with no formula, no definition text and no personal field; the page limits and the type of value beyond numeric(18,4) are local to the document.
why: The TSD gives Measure[] and the eleven members are the columns of measure_definition and measure_snapshot that a return can cite; a formula or a definition text in the answer would put a business wording into a contract.
read: TSD P9 T3.1 DF-RPT-031 to DF-RPT-052 and T-A.2; FSD P9 A2.7.3.1 BR-P9-007
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-reporting with the API owner
impact: An additive member is a minor change; a removed member is a new major version.

text: The decision-log read of rwb-decision is consumed at the decision base /api/recovery/decision/v1 under the published P7 decision-log contract and is faked here; the plan declares no C row for it, so it is a declared-and-faked consumed element and not a build dependency.
why: The return must trace a measure to its decision facts, the legacy story names the decision log, and the plan carries no C row for P7 in this key.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-001 AC1 and Data; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (C empty for RWB-P9-E8001-APP); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03 and DP-11
confirm: Owner of rwb-decision with the tech lead of rwb-reporting
impact: The decision facts arrive on one hop with a 2 s timeout; until the read is published the fake answers the same document.

text: A data-product filter and a dimension filter on the measure read are additive within major version 1, and the five parameters of TSD P9 T-A.2 keep their names measure, product, route, from and to.

confirm: API owner with the reporting owner

text: No file element is declared for the return: the 07:30 Power BI refresh and the INT-19 extract named by the FSD leave by the removed lake path, and any future regulator delivery is a new story with its own contract.
why: Architecture v5 removes INT-19 and INT-20 and DP-17 states that reporting reads from events into rwb-reporting with a gap where a story needs lake data; no source names a replacement file channel.
read: FSD P9 A2.7.2 and A2.1 AC-ALT-P9-001-02; TSD P9 T5.1; _work/msr/context/P9.md; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17
confirm: Solution architect with the BI owner
